tasks.title: Build repeatable static-enemy scaling test
tasks.description: Create a controlled performance benchmark using fixed stationary enemy counts and positions, consistent settling time and capture duration, with active idle enemy systems explicitly documented.
tasks.why_it_matters: Creates a clean performance baseline before pathfinding, combat, and defenses are introduced.
acceptance_criteria: Test setup can be reproduced reliably.
Enemy counts and spawn positions are fixed and documented.
Settling time and capture duration are consistent.
Active idle systems are explicitly documented.
Results are directly comparable between runs.
context: Use fixed enemy counts and fixed positions.
Use a consistent settling time and capture duration.
Explicitly document which idle enemy systems remain active.

tasks.title: Lazy allocate Artillery projectile-path ISM instances
tasks.description: Move Artillery projectile-path ISM allocation out of Construction Script and allocate instances lazily only when trajectory visualisation requires them.
tasks.why_it_matters: Current construction cost scales with every Artillery spawned and can hit Blueprint runaway-loop protection at high counts.
acceptance_criteria: No projectile-path ISM instances are allocated during normal Artillery construction.
Trajectory display grows the reusable instance pool only when required.
Previously allocated instances are retained and reused.
High-count Artillery benchmarks no longer hit this construction-script failure mode.
context: The current code path caused a crash during performance benchmarking.
Projectile-path ISM allocation is temporarily disabled so benchmarking can continue.
decisions: Do not treat as an immediate blocker while the visualisation path remains disabled.
tasks.promotion_criteria: Move to Ready when Artillery trajectory visualisation needs to be restored or the disabled path prevents representative testing.

tasks.title: Investigate Shooter and Brute static Game Thread cost
tasks.description: Compare static Game Thread cost for BaseClass, Brute, and Shooter using equivalent Unreal Insights captures.
tasks.why_it_matters: Shooter and Brute scale substantially worse than the base/other enemy classes before AI movement is active.
acceptance_criteria: Capture comparable Unreal Insights traces for BaseClass, Brute, and Shooter.
Identify the major Game Thread deltas between the three cases.
Produce at least one concrete follow-up hypothesis or task.
context: At 400 static actors: BaseClass ~31 ms GT, Brute ~49 ms GT, Shooter ~60 ms GT.
Compare traces under identical static benchmark conditions.
tasks.promotion_criteria: Move to Ready once the static-enemy benchmark setup is stable enough for directly comparable traces.

history.note: Expanded to compare Shooter and Brute against BaseClass.

tasks.title: Prototype and benchmark rigid-part 3D enemy
tasks.description: Build a deliberately simple rigid-part 3D enemy from a small hierarchy of static-mesh components, animate it without skeletal animation, and benchmark it against skeletal baselines.
tasks.why_it_matters: Tests whether simple static-mesh animation can preserve a 3D workflow while substantially reducing skeletal-animation cost at large enemy counts.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark identical actor counts in the existing performance-test level.
Compare normal animated skeletal enemies.
Compare dormant/no-animation skeletal baseline.
Compare the rigid-part static-mesh prototype.
Make a clear go/no-go decision on whether the performance gain justifies deeper work.
context: Start with ordinary Static Mesh Components rather than ISM/HISM.
Use the existing performance-test level and identical actor counts.
decisions: Do not design the production animation system until the performance hypothesis is validated.
Do not jump directly to ISM/HISM architecture.

history.note: Initially framed as a P2 static-mesh comparison.
Refined into a focused rigid-part 3D benchmark.

tasks.title: Explore centralized enemy update scheduling
tasks.description: Explore reducing per-enemy Tick/AI scaling by staggering expensive updates before considering any fully centralized simulation.
tasks.why_it_matters: Could reduce per-enemy update cost without replacing the existing Actor/Character architecture.
acceptance_criteria: Identify which expensive enemy updates are candidates for staggering.
Prototype a simple staggered-update approach.
Measure whether it improves scaling enough to justify further work.
Avoid committing to a full centralized enemy simulation unless evidence supports it.
context: Revisit after the rigid static-mesh benchmark.
Start with staggered expensive updates rather than a full centralized enemy simulation.
decisions: Preserve the current Actor/Character architecture for the first experiment.
Treat full centralized simulation as a later option, not the starting point.
tasks.promotion_criteria: Review after T062 and current performance investigations clarify whether per-enemy update scheduling is a significant scaling constraint.
